standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a node via the completed local ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 4678-4679: being a node is expressed through the completed local ring (the normal form kappa[[s, t]]/(st)), so an isomorphism of completions preserves it.

core_obligations: Reduction to the algebraic closure (proof lines 4669-4671): by lemma-node-field-extension one may base change to the algebraic closure of k, after which the residue fields of x and y are k.

Isomorphism of completions (lines 4673-4678): for an etale morphism with equal residue fields, the induced map on completed local rings O_{X,x}^ -> O_{Y,y}^ is an isomorphism (etale-lemma-characterize-etale-completions or more-algebra-lemma-flat-unramified).

Conclusion (lines 4678-4679): the node property is defined through the isomorphism class of the completed local ring (the normal form kappa[[s, t]]/(st) of lemma-nodal-algebraic), hence x is a node if and only if y is a node, and closedness is preserved along etale morphisms of 1-dimensional locally algebraic schemes.
proof_roadmap: Base change to the algebraic closure using the field-extension lemma.
Identify the completed local rings via the etale-completion lemma.
Read off the equivalence from the completed-ring definition of a node.
difficulty_reason: Stability lemma (statement 4661-4667, proof 4669-4679): nodes of 1-dimensional locally algebraic schemes are stable under etale morphisms - the proof reduces to the algebraic closure, identifies the completions through the standard etale-completion lemmas, and concludes from the completed-ring definition; the first step rests on the published lemma-node-field-extension (recorded in the notes). H2: short reduction argument.
